title: Lower-stack fault sources do not map one-to-one to agent-visible faults or final outcomes.
text: The source-mapping study contains 3,600 faulted and 180 clean executions. Of the 3,600 faulted executions, 36.0% have no recorded consumption symptom. Among 15,882 applied MAS faults, 89.4% have a recorded consequence and 80.2% fail the task. The 1,457 successful runs with a recorded consequence separate propagation from final failure.
caveat: Source-mapping fixtures and MAS task executions are distinct studies. A, M and O measure exposure, propagation and outcome separately.

title: Silent failures concentrate in faults that preserve a processable message.
text: There are 1,722 silent failures among 8,335 detection-complete failures (20.7%). The silent-failure rate is 76.2% for partial-content faults and 26.3% for semantic corruption. Partial-content faults account for 69.6% of all silent failures.
caveat: The denominator is detection-complete failures. The same 1,722 events are 15.6% of 11,022 detection-complete injected executions. A correct answer string alone may not satisfy the evidence contract.

title: Fault impact depends on whether the affected information remains recoverable.
text: I2 requests, I3 observations and I4 evidence handoffs expose different recovery opportunities. In the matched Admin Sequential/Hierarchical DeepSeek cohort, 82 of 110 I3-loss runs obtain a later table and 74 succeed; all 28 without a later table fail.
caveat: Position comparisons use matched tasks, models, topologies and repetitions with actual exposure. An intact direct edge can forward the same pre-interception evidence; it is not a new observation.

title: The most harmful communication fault changes with task context.
text: Under Flat, Shopping fails in 99.6% of semantic-corruption runs versus 53.0% of partial-content runs. SWE shows 3.1% versus 100.0%, TAC 33.3% versus 100.0%, and Reddit 66.7% versus 97.7%.
caveat: These descriptive profiles reflect information dependencies and task-specific evaluation contracts. They do not establish a universal task-complexity ranking.

title: Flat improves fault tolerance when its additional path still carries the required evidence.
text: Matched I4 non-delivery comparisons show a 66.5–66.6 percentage-point gain for Flat; evidence-handoff corruption shows 41.3–42.3 points. Gains are small at I2 and I3, before the alternate path has obtained the required evidence.
caveat: Paired effects use both-applied, known-outcome comparisons within the position-extension study. The case links below illustrate I4 non-delivery in the common matrix.

title: Changing the LLM provides limited recovery from communication faults.
text: Across 1,408 common faulted units, model switching rescues 0.2–4.5% of baseline failures, compared with 19.3–27.0% for switching to Flat. Rescue-set overlap is low (Jaccard 0–0.047).
caveat: All nine model–topology configurations share the matched cohort. These are deployed configurations, not a controlled model-size ablation; individual replay cases do not estimate the paired effect.

title: Effective protection must match the failed dependency and retain access to trustworthy evidence.
text: Of 106 baseline failures in the main mechanism comparison, execution protection uniquely rescues 67.9% and evidence protection 32.1%, with no overlap. Targeted checks remove incorrect intermediate acceptance; persistent recovery faults or shared-scope exposure can defeat combined protection.
caveat: The historical protection study (1,098 executions), targeted Shopping checks (432), Reddit recovery (162), and recovery-boundary study (288) have separate denominators. Fresh evidence acquisition still shares the underlying backend.
